58001.text: Airflow describes how molecules flow around an object. Which of the following is the name of the phenomenon that causes the low pressure on the upper surface of the wing during two-dimensional airflow?

58002.text: Which of the following is the distance measured along the chord line between the leading edge and the trailing edge?
options: The maximum thickness of the wing.

58003.text: What is the angle between the chord line and the relative wind called?

58004.text: Which of the following is perpendicular to the lift and parallel to the drag on an aerofoil section?
options: The upper surface of the aerofoil section.

58005.text: In straight and level flight, the air flowing over the upper surface of the wing, compared with the air flowing along its lower surface:
options: The air flowing over the upper surface of the wing has a lower pressure.

58006.text: In which phase of flight does wing tip vortex development begin?
options: During rotation, while lift is being generated
While moving the flaps to a lower position
While adjusting take-off power during take-off
The moment the aircraft starts moving on the runway
As soon as the aircraft starts moving

58007.text: Which of the following is correct regarding the relationship between wing span and induced drag?
options: Induced drag is inversely proportional to the aspect ratio.
Induced drag is directly proportional to the wing span.
Induced drag is not related to the aspect ratio.
As the wing span increases, induced drag first increases and then decreases.
Induced drag is directly proportional to the square of the wing span.

58008.text: What is the boundary layer on aircraft wings?
options: A thin layer in which the air molecules close to the wing surface slow down
A layer of ice forming on the upper surface of the wing
A dense layer of air forming on the lower surface of the wing
The area where the airflow over the wing speeds up
increase the lift coefficient so that the aircraft can fly at low speeds.
provide a nose-up movement during take-off.
The approach speed is independent of the flap configuration.
reduce the lift coefficient in order to slow the aircraft down.

58010.text: An aircraft that has deviated from its flight path due to turbulence is described as positively stable in which of the following cases?
options: When it returns to its original position without pilot intervention.
When it continues to deviate in the direction of the disturbance until opposing forces are applied that balance the forces that caused the deviation.
When it returns to its former position with pilot intervention.
When it deviates even further from its original position after the disturbance.
When it maintains the new flight path after the deviation.

58011.text: The tendency of an aircraft to generate forces that return it to its original flight condition after its steady flight condition has been disturbed is called:

58012.text: Which of the following indicates that an aircraft has static stability?
options: It tends to return by itself to its previous position when the force is removed.
Fewer pilot inputs are needed to control it.
It will not enter a spin.

58013.text: Which of the following surfaces provides directional stability to the aircraft?

58014.text: Which of the following correctly defines the purpose of the trim tab?
options: To eliminate the loads transmitted from the control surfaces to the control column, depending on the flight attitude being flown.
To create loads that give the pilot a feel for the control surfaces at high speeds.
To increase the effectiveness of the control surfaces.
To make it harder for the pilot to move the control surfaces.
To increase control effectiveness only at high speeds.

58015.text: About which axis does an aircraft perform a pitching movement?

58016.text: Which of the following correctly defines the lateral axis of an aircraft?
options: The line passing through the centre of gravity, parallel to the line joining the wing tips.
The line perpendicular to the longitudinal axis, passing through the ¼ chord point of the wing root.
The line passing through the wing tips.
The line perpendicular to the direction of airflow, passing through the centre of pressure (CP).
The line passing through the exact middle of the wing root.

58017.text: Yaw control is used to control which movement of the aircraft?
options: Movement of the nose to the right or left
Movement of the nose up or down
Movement of the wings up or down
Rolling movement to the right or left

58018.text: Why is the vertical tail profile designed to be symmetrical?
options: To prevent yaw about the normal axis
To increase yaw about the lateral axis
To prevent pitching about the lateral axis
To prevent surface drag about the normal axis
To prevent rolling about the vertical axis

58019.text: Which speed is the upper limit of the normal operating speed range?

58020.text: How does the mass of an aircraft affect the Manoeuvring Load Diagram?
options: An increase in mass increases the limit manoeuvring load factors.
A decrease in mass reduces the limit manoeuvring load factors.
An increase in mass does not change the limit manoeuvring speed.
A decrease in mass reduces the aerodynamic performance of the aircraft.
An increase in mass allows the aircraft to reach higher speeds.

58021.text: What does the VFE speed mean?
options: The maximum speed at which the flaps can be used safely
The speed that must never be exceeded

58022.text: Which of the following correctly defines the VNE speed?
options: The maximum permissible airspeed at which the aeroplane can fly.
The maximum speed at which the flaps may be deployed.
The speed that must not be exceeded under any circumstances, except in a dive.
The maximum speed that can be reached in flight manoeuvres in conditions close to the stall.

58023.text: How can the asymmetric blade effect that an aircraft encounters at low speeds be reduced?
options: By keeping the propeller RPM constant.

58024.text: How is the "torque reaction" that occurs while the aircraft's propeller is rotating managed?
options: By changing the propeller's direction of rotation

58025.text: Which of the following is not a type of propeller?

58026.text: What is the purpose of the "blade twist" used in propellers?
options: To increase the aerodynamic efficiency of the propellers
To make the propellers rotate faster
To enable the aircraft to climb to higher altitudes

58027.text: Which of the following is not one of the methods used against icing on propellers?

58028.text: How is the load factor determined in level flight?
options: It is the ratio of the lift force to the weight force.
It is the ratio of the thrust force to drag.
It is the ratio of the lift force to the bank angle.
It is the ratio of the weight force to drag.
It is the ratio of the weight force to the lift force.

58029.text: During a steady climb at constant speed, ...........
options: the lift force is less than the weight force.
the lift force is greater than the weight force.

58030.text: How is the load factor determined in a banked coordinated turn?
options: In banked coordinated turns, the load factor is independent of the bank angle
